subject: Paytone priority: urgent corrective plan for reserved QPS deficit and 5xx spike
messages:
From: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@paytone.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: ops@paytone.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: production 5xx + timeouts — hitting reserved capacity

Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and end-to-end latencies at ~13:40 PST. Our dashboard shows queued requests growing and reserved throughput for our account dropping below the committed QPS. Below are the immediate symptoms:
- Spike in 5xx from 0.02% -> 2.4% over 20 minutes
- P95 latency increased from 120ms -> 1.8s
- Token throughput plateau despite steady traffic (no large client-side changes)

I've attached the error snapshot and a short log extract (paytone_error_snapshot_20261122.log). This is customer-facing traffic in production and we are seeing some user sessions time out. Can you confirm this is on your side and what immediate mitigations you can enable?

Claire Zhao
Director, Core Platform
Paytone

Attachments: paytone_error_snapshot_20261122.log (log)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@paytone.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example, logan_wright@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production 5xx + timeouts — hitting reserved capacity

Claire — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We see correlated alerts on our side for Paytone's reservation consuming more tokens than expected and a growing KV cache backlog. Immediate plan (15–60 min):
1) Route a small percentage (10%) of Paytone traffic to our burst fleet to relieve queueing.
2) Enable prefix/KV cache warm by pinning recent contexts for high-frequency keys.
3) Temporarily reduce max context length for non-critical routes to drop per-request tokens.
4) Open an ops bridge — rishi and the infra team are on it.

We'll confirm once the burst routing is live. Can your team stand up a brief canary (5–10%) to verify correctness while we lift the backlog?

–Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 14:28:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: production 5xx + timeouts — hitting reserved capacity

Team — quick diagnostic from the bridge:
- Root cause signal: sudden increase in long-context batch jobs from a tenant in the shared pool that spilled into Paytone's reservation window. KV cache GC lagged because of a large streaming workload; that raised contention and injected headroom pressure.
- Immediate mitigations executed:
  * Throttled noisy neighbor workloads in the shared pool (5 min).
  * Enabled burst routing for Paytone (activated at 14:23 PST).
  * Switched Paytone's production route to the quantized model variant for non-critical endpoints (saves ~30% tokens/latency).
  * Cleared stale KV entries and warmed prefixes for top-200 keys.
- Early results: queue depth down 65%, P95 latency back to ~260ms, 5xx rate falling toward baseline.

Important ask for executive approval: the burst routing consumed ~1.6x of Paytone's monthly reserved allowance in the last 40 minutes. To avoid an SLA credit event and keep production stable through the next 36 hours, we need approval for 48 hours of temporary burst capacity and a one-time credit extension while we run a canary fallback and a scheduled remediation window.

I've attached a short diagnostic snippet showing kernel/queue metrics (diagnostic_snippet.txt).

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: diagnostic_snippet.txt (txt)

From: logan_wright@redwood.example
To: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@paytone.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Paytone action plan and next steps (canary + temporary burst)

Claire — thanks for working with us on the bridge. Short plan and asks: 
- What we did (already in effect): burst routing (10–25% split), quantized model fallback for non-critical routes, KV-prefix warm.
- Next 24 hours: run a staged canary at 10% -> 25% to validate behavior for business-critical endpoints; monitor for regressions.
- Requests from Paytone: please confirm which endpoints are business-critical and which can safely go to the quantized path. If you can send that list in the next 30 minutes, we will program the routing rules.
- Procurement: our team will need quick approval for temporary burst credits. If procurement can sign a 48-hour amendment, we can avoid throttling and maintain user experience. DocuSign link for the amendment is: https://docusign.net/DocuSign/external/ABC123

I'll keep you updated every 2 hours and set up a 15-min standup at the top of each hour until the backlog normalizes.

Logan Wright
Customer Success — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, olga_petrov@redwood.example
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example, logan_wright@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 16:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec ask: approve 48-hr burst authorization and one-time credit extension for Paytone

Marissa / Olga — brief executive summary and ask:
- Impact: Paytone (priority account, contract PT-78-B) experienced a reserved throughput shortfall caused by cross-tenant long-context jobs spilling into reserved windows. Customer-facing 5xx and high latencies observed between 13:40–14:20 PST.
- Actions taken: ops throttled noisy neighbor, activated burst routing, applied quantized fallback, warmed KV prefixes. Metrics improving but still reliant on burst capacity to return to steady state.
- Ask: approve a 48-hour burst capacity allocation (emergency burst) and a one-time credit extension to avoid an SLA credit event while we complete remediation and a production canary. Estimated cost exposure: ~$28k incremental infra spend for 48 hours; estimated credit impact if SLA triggers: much larger and damages relationship.
- Follow-ups: engineering will run a tail-latency remediation task (24–72 hrs) and product will provide a routing hardening patch to prevent cross-tenant spillover.

Please confirm approval or next steps. If approved I will sign and route the DocuSign amendment (link above) and alert finance for expedited reconciliation.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@paytone.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.example
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Paytone action plan and next steps (canary + temporary burst)

Logan / Karthik — thank you for the rapid response and the clear plan. We will: 
- Share the list of business-critical endpoints in the next 20 minutes (ops@paytone.com is on this thread).
- Execute the 10% canary now and report results after 30 min.
- Approve the 48-hour amendment via DocuSign (signing now) to avoid service disruption.

Appreciate the proactive communication and hourly updates. Please keep execs in the loop if we see any regression.

Claire
